propositions: Dual vocabulary of 'Success Criteria' and 'Acceptance Criteria' in reviewer prompts introduces noise by suggesting a distinction that criteria routing does not enforce, pooling them under a single bar.
Reviewer prompt files use inconsistent terminology ('success criteria', 'acceptance criteria', and bare 'SC' tokens) that must be standardized to 'acceptance criteria' throughout.
The criteria routing index and generated criteria guide are downstream artifacts that perpetuate the dual vocabulary and must be regenerated after source prompts are updated.
Renaming must preserve deliberate exclusions: generic English in plan_review_T2.md describing pilot success metrics, and out-of-scope definition-of-done wording in verifier prompts.
Editing criteria_routing.json rotates the regver stamp, invalidating outstanding attestations, which is now safe because the grandfathering prerequisite ticket has merged.
Registry version must rotate as a side effect of the routing edit, proven by capturing both pre- and post-edit computed versions at runtime rather than against hardcoded literals.
